release_summary.summary: The problem (PD-1) was defined from authoritative tool data: dispute tickets doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-03). Two stakeholder-proposed causes - slow ticket response (SH-CS's original request, CL-01) and a tariff change - were ruled out by evidence (SLA met per E-04; no tariff change per E-05/E-06). Billing-db shows 59% of disputed bills used ACTUAL meter reads (E-02), pointing to a suspected but unconfirmed August billing import validation rule change (H-RULE-CHANGE-IMPORT-ERROR) as the primary cause; the remaining 41% ESTIMATED-read bucket was initially linked to a route-completion shortfall (E-01, 88% vs 95% target), but newer AMI evidence (E-11/F-08) shows most of those same bills actually had on-time AMI reads rejected by billing import for high consumption, contradicting that narrative. The release delivers three items - dispute-volume monitoring, route-completion monitoring, and a route-priority/overtime update (gated on SH-FIELD's runtime confirmation per K-DISPATCH) - but releases no fix to the billing rule itself; manual rule correction and re-billing require Billing Operations under K-BILLWRITE and were not performed. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (nothing held back) because release-time semantic verification flagged two unresolved issues - the release only covers the secondary driver while the primary root cause remains unconfirmed (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION still OPEN), and the problem narrative for the ESTIMATED bucket is contradicted by later evidence - alongside several other tracked limitations around data completeness, handoff validity, tool health, and an unverified staffing-to-shortfall causal link.
key_points: The problem was defined (PD-1) from CRM data: dispute tickets roughly doubled from a 590-610/month baseline to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 and stayed elevated (E-03/F-03).

Two stakeholder-proposed causes were tested and ruled out with authoritative data: slow ticket handling (SH-CS's framing, CL-01) is contradicted because response times are within SLA, median 1.6 days vs 3.0-day target (E-04/F-04); and a tariff change is contradicted by zero logged tariff changes (E-05/F-05, corroborated by SH-BILL's E-06).

The remaining 41% ESTIMATED-read bucket was initially attributed to a route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01/F-01, linked to SH-FIELD's staffing claim E-07), but later AMI data (E-11/F-08) shows 95.5% of those same bills actually had on-time AMI reads that were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION by billing import, not missing reads - directly contradicting the route-completion narrative and H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.

Two stakeholder-proposed causes - slow ticket response (SH-CS's original request, CL-01) and a tariff change - were ruled out by evidence (SLA met per E-04; no tariff change per E-05/E-06). Billing-db shows 59% of disputed bills used ACTUAL meter reads (E-02), pointing to a suspected but unconfirmed August billing import validation rule change (H-RULE-CHANGE-IMPORT-ERROR) as the primary cause; the remaining 41% ESTIMATED-read bucket was initially linked to a route-completion shortfall (E-01, 88% vs 95% target), but newer AMI evidence (E-11/F-08) shows most of those same bills actually had on-time AMI reads rejected by billing import for high consumption, contradicting that narrative. The release delivers three items - dispute-volume monitoring, route-completion monitoring, and a route-priority/overtime update (gated on SH-FIELD's runtime confirmation per K-DISPATCH) - but releases no fix to the billing rule itself; manual rule correction and re-billing require Billing Operations under K-BILLWRITE and were not performed. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (nothing held back) because release-time semantic verification flagged two unresolved issues - the release only covers the secondary driver while the primary root cause remains unconfirmed (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION still OPEN), and the problem narrative for the ESTIMATED bucket is contradicted by later evidence - alongside several other tracked limitations around data completeness, handoff validity, tool health, and an unverified staffing-to-shortfall causal link.
